title: The Late Alibi
premise: Juniper Ishikawa, a concierge at the fading Hotel Meridian, has spent years perfecting the art of being unnoticed—until guest Marguerite Vale vanishes, leaving behind a diary whose entries continue for three weeks after her disappearance. As police close the case as a runaway, Juniper notices the handwriting shifts and realizes someone is forging the diary to establish an alibi for the night of the annual Vale family anniversary dinner, where the will will finally be read. Following the forged entries through the hotel's forgotten corners, Juniper hunts for Odile, the family's supposedly dead housekeeper who witnessed the original crime years ago. At the anniversary dinner, Juniper exposes the forgery and produces Odile—alive, hidden in plain sight as the hotel's night cleaner—forcing a confession from Marguerite's brother before justice can be served outside the courtroom.
about_author: Cyrus Sterling is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent a decade collecting the secrets guests leave behind in lobbies and elevators. They write mysteries about the invisible people who keep grand buildings running—and what happens when one of them stops looking away.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unnoticed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. We meet the concierge who reads guests like weather systems: arrivals, affairs, debts, despair. Marguerite Vale checks in for a long stay, nervous, asking odd questions about the hotel's history. When Marguerite fails to appear for two days, Juniper is asked to pack her room and finds the diary. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Police declare Marguerite a voluntary runaway; the family seems oddly relieved. Reading the diary, Juniper finds entries dated after the disappearance—but the final pages describe things Marguerite couldn't have known, including Juniper herself. Emotional beat: the thrill of being seen colliding with dread.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Will Be Served
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Vale family books the ballroom for their annual dinner, where patriarch Edmund Vale will announce changes to the will. Juniper observes the brother, Alistair, rehearsing grief badly, and a lawyer who flinches at the word 'witness.' Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Housekeeper Saw
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with diary excerpts. Old staff records reveal Odile Marchand, housekeeper for thirty years, officially dead since 1998—the same year Marguerite's mother died. The diary's forged entries keep circling back to 'the woman in the east stairwell.' Emotional beat: grief for a erased life fueling Juniper's resolve.

chapters.title: Ink and Pressure
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Consulting a retired graphologist living at the hotel, Juniper confirms the late entries are traced over time—a manufactured alibi built page by page. Someone needed proof Marguerite was alive after a specific date. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing the diary was written for an audience of one: the future.

chapters.title: The East Stairwell
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the diary's geography, Juniper explores the sealed service corridors and finds signs of habitation: tinned food, a blanket, a child's photograph of the Vale household. Someone lives—or lived—in the building's bones. Emotional beat: claustrophobic intimacy with the hotel's hidden heart.

chapters.title: Alistair's Alibi
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV (brief, unreliable). He rehearses his dinner speech, convinced the forged diary protects him from suspicion in his mother's death years ago. He searches Marguerite's room, certain she found Odile first. Emotional beat: arrogance curdling into panic as he realizes someone else is reading the same clues.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Swept at Night
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finally confronts the night cleaner, Marta—who removes her wig and admits she is Odile, hiding in the only place no one looks: plain sight. She saw Alistair kill his mother but was declared dead to silence her testimony. Emotional beat: recognition between two invisible women.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Alistair raises his glass to the family's continuity while the will is read. Juniper engineers a moment: the diary projected beside its ink analysis, then Odile walking into the light. Alistair breaks, confessing both deaths. Emotional beat: cathartic exposure, justice arriving without handcuffs.

chapters.title: Concierge, Still
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Weeks later: Odile testifies safely, Marguerite returns from hiding, and the Meridian begins restoring its forgotten corridors. Juniper declines credit, returning to the desk—but now guests notice her noticing them, and she lets them. Emotional beat: chosen visibility; invisibility becomes a gift given, not a sentence served.
